subject: About filtering filter samples based on coverage

messages.author: 15c078609fced006
messages.subject: About filtering filter samples based on coverage
parts:
Hi, Altuna

In order to reduce the PCR bias, I have used the methylKit function "filterByCoverage" with the following settings:

methyf = filterByCoverage(methy,lo.count=10,lo.perc=NULL, hi.count=500,hi.perc=NULL)

After the application of this function, I could detect that still there some coverages with values above 500. Could you please tell me if this function just remove the values above the given threshold or an algorithm/criterion is applied to decide whether or not a particular coverage is an "outlier"?

Best regards,

Robersy

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: About filtering filter samples based on coverage
parts:
Hi Robersy,
It is a simple cutoff, the coverages shouldn't be above that cutoff, and the code is pretty simple, the basics are below and it works on the test data in the package:

data(methylKit) # get example data
methylObj=methylRawList.obj[[1]] # get a methylRaw object

# code from the filterByCoverage function
hi.count=500
lo.count=20
data=getData(methylObj)
data=data[data$coverage>=lo.count,]
data=data[data$coverage<hi.count,]
           

new("methylRaw",data,sample.id=methylObj@sample.id,
                     assembly=methylObj@assembly,
                     context=methylObj@context,resolution=methylObj@resolution)


Maybe you can check if the coverage column of your data is numeric, or if there is sth out of the ordinary since you read data from BSMAP output.

Best,
Altuna
